name: Tarun Ramprakash
headline: Aerospace researcher — CFD and solver development
summaryShort: I build the solvers that make transonic aerodynamics computable — and study where they stop being trustworthy.
summaryLong: I spend most of my working hours doing something that looks, from the outside, like staring at numbers until they behave: writing the solvers that predict how air moves over a wing, then hunting for the exact point where they stop telling the truth. My MSc at Cranfield was built around that second half — not getting a transonic solver to converge, but finding precisely where it couldn't, and why.

The same habit has followed me from wind tunnels to CFD clusters to a UAV that once carried 30 kg to 19,024 ft, which is a very good way to stop being careless about what a model actually claims. These days that mostly means asking which setting in a simulation is quietly deciding the answer.

Off the clock I'm usually chasing a football or a shuttlecock around a court, badly, and I'm told by everyone who knows me that I disappear into work for stretches that don't count as healthy. I'm working on that. The solvers, less so.
availability: Open to collaboration — academic or industrial
